Incorporating the April 2023 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey, the tone shifts more cautious than the FOMC statement alone suggests. The SLOOS shows broad-based tightening of lending standards and terms across C&I and commercial real estate (wider spreads, lower LTVs, higher DSCR) and tighter standards for consumer credit (auto, residential real estate, HELOCs, subprime), with banks citing economic outlook, funding costs, deposit outflows, and liquidity positions. Demand weakened for C&I use cases (plant/equipment, M&A, inventory, A/R), and banks expect further tightening; foreign banks reported similar moves. This reinforces the FSR’s noted vulnerabilities and the Committee’s warning that tighter credit will weigh on activity and hiring, despite a resilient banking system and strong labor market. Net effect: more negative than mildly cautious.
